newsitem.title: GERMANY: Firm dollar deters Bremen cotton buyers.
newsitem.headline: Firm dollar deters Bremen cotton buyers.

text.p: European cotton consumers are buying hand to mouth amid dollar-induced price strength and limited nearby supply, a fortnightly market report from the Bremen Cotton Exchange said on Monday.
The same factors slowed trade in distant months.
Cotton stocks as of Feb 7 totalled 34,513 bales, up 14,786 on the previous fortnight but well below 107,258 recorded a year earlier.
The Exchange reported upland cotton trades in Central Asian standards 1-4, East Africans and Argentine high/medium grades for 1997 dates.
In the longstaple sector, it reported trades in Egyptian Giza 75 and 77 for the first half of 1997 as well as transactions in Israel-Pima for the second quarter.
